newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Jamaica's balance of payments worsens.
newsitem.headline: Jamaica's balance of payments worsens.

text.p: Jamaica's current account deficit totalled US$186.9 million for the first 11 months of 1996, down sharply from a deficit of US$80.6 million two months earlier but US$21.3 million more than the deficit for the first 11 months of 1995, according to figures issued by the Bank of Jamaica Wednesday.

The trade deficit over the 11 months hit US$1.32 billion, US$128.8 million more than in the same period in 1995. Exports stood at US$1.27 billion as of November, while imports rose to US$2.59 billion.
A worsening in the trade balance and a spate of overseas borrowing to purchase imports and write down expensive local debt were blamed for the sharp deterioration in the balance of payments.

Tourism earnings for the first 11 monmths of 1996 rose 5.16 percent, from US$940.8 million in 1995 to US$989.3 million last year. Remittances, which until now had kept the balance of payments in the black, fell by US$38.2 million over last year to US$422.5 million.
Private capital inflows including loans secured overseas stood at US$530 million, up from US$230.6 million as of November 1995.
